title: Local top-wedge determinant modules and descent of supplied tensor comparisons
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A finite projective module means a direct summand of a finite free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Exterior powers and their pure wedges are those of [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], and tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every finite projective $E$, let $D_R(E)$ be its exterior-algebra annihilator of $E$ [def-trf-projective-determinant-module]. Fix finitely many $f_a\in R$ generating the unit ideal such that $E_{f_a}$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with a basis of length $n_a$; localizations are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Put $L_a=\bigwedge^{n_a}_{R_{f_a}}E_{f_a}$. On any nonzero overlap $R_{f_af_b}$ the two ranks agree, and the exterior powers of the identity of $E_{f_af_b}$ identify $(L_a)_{f_b}$ with $(L_b)_{f_a}$; on a zero overlap the identification is the unique map. These identifications satisfy the cocycle equations. The modules $L_a$ with these transitions descend to a finite projective module $D$, locally free of rank one, canonically isomorphic to $D_R(E)$. Its chart identifications are induced by the exterior-algebra localization maps and the inclusion of the top exterior power. They are independent of the finite free cover and its refinements and commute with every further localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] $R\to S^{-1}R$, including localization at a multiplicative subset containing zero. For $E=0$ they give the canonical identification $D_R(0)=R$ taking the empty wedge to $1$.
More generally, let $E_1,E_2,E_3$ be finite projective $R$-modules and choose such a simultaneous finite free cover, with ranks $n_{k,a}$ and $L_{k,a}=\bigwedge^{n_{k,a}}(E_k)_{f_a}$. Suppose given $R_{f_a}$-linear isomorphisms $\lambda_a:L_{1,a}\otimes_{R_{f_a}}L_{2,a}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{3,a}$ that agree on every overlap under the preceding transitions and tensor localization. There is a unique $R$-linear isomorphism $\lambda:D_R(E_1)\otimes_R D_R(E_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_R(E_3)$ whose localizations are the $\lambda_a$. Its inverse descends the $\lambda_a^{-1}$. Refinement leaves this isomorphism unchanged, and its localization at any multiplicative subset is the unique isomorphism obtained by descending the localized family.

proof.text: Write $A=\bigwedge_R E$. The canonical map $A\to\bigwedge_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}E)$ is a module localization: on each graded piece this is [new-v2-generic-exterior-power-localization], and the direct-sum grading of [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] gives the assertion for $A$. Explicitly every element has finitely many homogeneous components, so their fraction representatives admit a common denominator; if an element maps to zero, finitely many annihilating denominators for its components have a product annihilating it. Multiplication of fractions agrees with wedge multiplication because this holds on pure wedges and extends by linearity. The maps for successive localizations agree on every pure wedge and on scalars, hence on the whole algebra.

source.place: Tag 0C6F, lemma-tensor-algebra-localization; degreewise localization and finite-support direct-sum assembly

proof.text: Choose generators $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ of $E$: the images under the given retraction of a finite free basis generate it. By bilinearity, $x\in D_R(E)$ means exactly $x\wedge e_i=0$ for every $i$. The map of step 1 therefore restricts to a localization $D_R(E)\to D_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}E)$. Indeed, write a target element as $x/s$. Each $x\wedge e_i$ vanishes after localization, so choose $u_i\in S$ annihilating it and put $u=\prod_i u_i$. Then $ux\in D_R(E)$ and $x/s=(ux)/(us)$. If an element of $D_R(E)$ maps to zero, a denominator annihilates it in $A$ and hence in the submodule $D_R(E)$. Denominators act invertibly in the target. These are precisely the fraction and equality properties of localization. This argument also applies when $t=0$ or $0\in S$.

source.place: Tag 0FJA, remark-determinant-as-socle: localization verification by finitely many annihilator equations

proof.text: For a free module $F$ with basis $v_1,\ldots,v_n$, expand an element of its exterior algebra uniquely as $x=\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}c_Iv_I$, using the graded decomposition and [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. For a fixed $j$, the terms of $x\wedge v_j$ with $j\notin I$ have distinct basis indices $I\cup\{j\}$ and coefficient $\pm c_I$. Thus $x\wedge v_j=0$ forces $c_I=0$ for every $I$ omitting $j$. Annihilation by all $v_j$ leaves exactly the full-index term; conversely its wedge with every generator is zero. Consequently the inclusion identifies $\bigwedge^n F$ with $D(F)$, free on the top wedge. This uses only units $\pm1$, so holds in characteristic two and over the zero ring. For $n=0$ it identifies the empty wedge with $1\in R$.

source.place: Tag 00DM, section-tensor-algebra, finite free exterior basis; socle calculation of Tag 0FJA

proof.text: Apply steps 2 and 3 to each chart to obtain canonical isomorphisms $\alpha_a:D_R(E)_{f_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_a$, characterized by equality of their images in the localized exterior algebra. On a nonzero overlap the two localized bases of $E$ have equal lengths by [lem-sfb-commutative-ring-invariant-basis-number]. Here localization of a basis remains a basis: extend the coordinate maps and their inverse by the fraction formula. The degreewise comparison of step 1 therefore identifies both localized $L_a,L_b$ with the same top exterior submodule. Their transition is $\alpha_b\alpha_a^{-1}$ after restriction. On a zero overlap all modules are zero and there is exactly one map. These descriptions give identity transitions and the cocycle equation by cancellation of consecutive $\alpha$'s.

source.place: Tags 0FJ9 and 0FJA, local top exterior descriptions; Algebra rank uniqueness on nonzero rings

proof.text: Take $D=D_R(E)$ with the chart maps $\alpha_a$. This realizes the prescribed descent datum, and each localization is free of rank one. The finite principal-cover criterion [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective] implies that $D$ is finite projective. To see the canonical character of descent, any other module $D'$ with these charts has a unique map to $D$: for $x\in D'$, its local images in $D_{f_a}$ agree, so [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] supplies a unique image in $D$. Uniqueness makes this assignment linear. Interchanging $D,D'$ supplies its inverse, since both composites are locally the identity and the same cover lemma detects equality. Thus this choice of $D$ gives the canonical isomorphism claimed.

source.place: Tag 0FJA, identification with determinant; Algebra Tags 00NX (lemma-finite-projective) and 00EK (lemma-cover-module)

proof.text: The chart comparison is independent of all basis choices because step 3 identifies the top exterior submodule by its inclusion, not by a chosen generator. For two covers, their pairwise intersections form a common principal refinement: if $\sum r_af_a=\sum s_bg_b=1$, then $\sum_{a,b}r_as_bf_ag_b=1$. On that refinement both chart systems are the restriction of the same exterior localization map, by steps 1 and 2. The injectivity assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] then makes their descended identifications equal. For any multiplicative subset $S$, step 2 identifies $S^{-1}D_R(E)$ with $D_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}E)$; step 1 shows on pure wedges that this identification commutes with every chart and successive localization. If $0\in S$ all modules are zero. If $E=0$, step 3 globally gives $D_R(0)=R$, with the required empty-wedge normalization.

source.place: Tag 0FJA, intrinsic socle model; cover independence expanded using Algebra Tag 00EK

proof.text: Put $P=D_R(E_1)\otimes_R D_R(E_2)$ and $Q=D_R(E_3)$. The chart maps already established and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] identify $P_{f_a}$ with $L_{1,a}\otimes L_{2,a}$ and $Q_{f_a}$ with $L_{3,a}$. For $p\in P$, form $q_a=\alpha_{3,a}^{-1}\lambda_a((\alpha_{1,a}\otimes\alpha_{2,a})(p/1))$. The assumed overlap agreement says exactly that the $q_a\in Q_{f_a}$ form a compatible family. By [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] they glue to a unique $q\in Q$; define $\lambda(p)=q$. Local linearity and uniqueness of gluing prove additivity and $R$-linearity. The localized map equals $\lambda_a$ on all fractions $p/f_a^k$, since it does on $p/1$ and both maps are $R_{f_a}$-linear. The injectivity clause of the cover lemma proves uniqueness of $\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 00DL, lemma-tensor-product-localization, and Tag 00EK, lemma-cover-module: elementwise descent of the supplied tensor map

proof.text: The inverses $\lambda_a^{-1}$ agree on overlaps, since the compatibility equation for $\lambda_a$ can be multiplied on both sides by the corresponding inverses. For each $q\in Q$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] to the compatible local preimages in $P_{f_a}$ to obtain a linear map $\mu:Q\to P$. The localizations of $\mu\lambda$ and $\lambda\mu$ are identities. Injectivity in that lemma gives $\mu\lambda=1_P$ and $\lambda\mu=1_Q$. Thus $\lambda$ is an isomorphism with precisely the asserted descended inverse.

source.place: Tag 00EK, lemma-cover-module: descent of inverse maps and local detection of equality

proof.text: If the given family is restricted to any finite principal refinement, the constructed $\lambda$ still has those localizations; the uniqueness argument of step 7 over the refinement leaves it unchanged. For $R\to S^{-1}R$, the images of the $f_a$ still generate the unit ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] and steps 1, 2 and 6, the localization of $\lambda$ has as its chart maps exactly the localized $\lambda_a$: on pure tensors this is the equality $(x/s)\otimes(y/t)\mapsto\lambda(x\otimes y)/(st)$ under the tensor comparison, and linearity gives it on all elements. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] over $S^{-1}R$ to obtain uniqueness of the descended map. Its inverse is the localization of $\mu$. This includes $0\in S$ and proves all asserted refinement and localization compatibilities.
